name: Ace-To-Six Lowball (Draw) Poker
description: Ace-To-Six Lowball (Draw) Poker is the single-draw implementation of ace-to-six lowball, where straights and flushes count against low hands.
deck: Standard 52-card deck (some tables allow one joker as a bug)

overview.description: Ace-To-Six Lowball (Draw) Poker is the single-draw implementation of ace-to-six lowball, where straights and flushes count against low hands.
overview.deck: Standard 52-card deck (some tables allow one joker as a bug)

history.origins: Ace-to-six lowball developed as a home-game lowball ranking in eastern United States and United Kingdom poker circles, then spread through parts of Europe.
timeline: 20th century: London and European rooms adopt ace-to-six low ranking.
Modern mixed games: Ace-to-six appears in specialist lowball and dealer's choice rotations.
history.cultural: Known as a traditional lowball format in London-style mixed poker.
history.evolution: Compared with ace-to-five, this form penalizes accidental straights and flushes, making low draws more demanding.

setup.players: Two to six players. As with other five-card draw lowball variants, the game is typically played in this range; with more than six players the deck can run short when many draw replacements, so six is a practical maximum. Play proceeds clockwise from the dealer's left.
setup.deck: Standard 52-card deck; optional joker bug in some house rules.
setup.dealing: Deal 5 cards face-down to each player.
setup.equipment: Deck, chips, dealer button, and blind markers if blind structure is used.

rules.objective: Make the lowest five-card hand by ace-to-six ranking.
rules.gameplay: Players contribute forced bets (ante or blinds), receive five down cards, complete first betting, perform a single draw (discard 0-5 then draw equal replacements, or stand pat), complete final betting, and go to showdown.
keyRules: Straights and flushes count and are bad for low ranking.
A-2-3-4-5 is a straight and therefore weak in this variant.
Hands are compared from highest card downward among low hands.

strategy.basic: Avoid draws that can complete a straight or flush by accident.
strategy.intermediate: Track outs that spoil lows, especially 5-completions to A-2-3-4 patterns.
strategy.advanced: Use pat lines selectively, since opponents also account for straight/flush contamination risk.
tips: A-2-3 starts can be awkward if they force straight-prone continuation cards.
A pat hand can be value or bluff depending on prior draw pattern.

variations.name: Single Draw Mainline
variations.description: Primary form: one draw round and two main betting rounds.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Mainline single-draw structure is already encoded in the base engine; no additional overrides are needed.

variations.name: Triple Draw Extension
variations.description: Three draw rounds with additional betting rounds as a table variation.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Triple-draw extension is noted as a descriptive table variant; specific engine overrides are not yet modeled.

scoring.description: Pot game; best low hand wins the pot at showdown.
scoring.winCondition: Lowest valid ace-to-six hand at showdown wins.

synthesis.shortDescription: Single-draw lowball where aces are low and straights/flushes are penalties.
